# Define tutorial packaging format

## Description

Defines the packaging format in which curated tutorials are authored and shipped:
tutorial metadata, pinned image references, and a validation manifest. The format
makes tutorials versioned and testable independently of Dashboard releases, and it
is the contract that the Dashboard tutorial gallery's launch mechanics and tutorial
validation build against. This epic defines and validates the format; the six
curated tutorials themselves are authored as separate content deliverables outside
this scope. The normative specification of the format is authored here and is the
single authoritative definition of it; user-facing documentation topics that teach
the contribution process reference this specification and are authored in the
documentation work stream, not here.

## Scope

- Specify the packaging format for curated getting-started content:
  - metadata describing each packaged item (identity, target journey, and launch
    characteristics) covering both launch kinds — notebook-based items, which launch
    by opening a workbench, and pipeline-based items, which launch by importing a
    pipeline;
  - pinned image references (the workbench images a packaged item runs on);
  - a validation manifest that allows a packaged item to be tested against a
    platform release.
- Define versioning semantics for packaged content so content releases are
  decoupled from Dashboard releases.
- Validate the format with a minimal format-validation stub: a small fixture that
  exercises the metadata, a pinned image reference, and a validation manifest. The
  stub is validation scaffolding only — it demonstrates the format and is not a
  usable deliverable.
- Author the normative format specification — the authoritative definition of the
  format, including the author-facing packaging reference — so that content authors
  can package new material without bespoke guidance. This epic owns the normative
  spec; user-facing documentation topics that teach packaging as part of the
  contribution process reference the spec and are authored in the documentation
  work stream, not here.

Out of scope: authoring the six curated content items; the Dashboard gallery UI and
launch mechanics; user-facing documentation topics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the format specification, an item packaged per the format carries metadata,
  pinned image references, and a validation manifest, and can be versioned and
  tested independently of Dashboard releases.
- Given notebook-based content packaged per the format, its metadata is sufficient
  to launch it by opening a workbench with its notebook; given pipeline-based
  content packaged per the format, its metadata is sufficient to launch it by
  importing its pipeline.
- Given the minimal format-validation stub, the validation manifest executes
  against the current release and reports a pass/fail result.
- Given only the normative format specification, a content author can package new
  material without additional bespoke guidance.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): defines the tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images,
  validation manifest) so tutorials are versioned and testable independently of
  Dashboard releases.
- Enables HLR-1 and HLR-2: the gallery launch mechanics and the curated tutorials
  are built against this format.

# Dashboard tutorial gallery with one-click launch

## Description

Adds a curated tutorial gallery to the Dashboard. Users browse the gallery and
launch a tutorial into their own project with one click: notebook tutorials open a
workbench preloaded with the tutorial notebook, and pipeline tutorials import the
pipeline into the project. The gallery reads tutorials packaged per the tutorial
packaging format, so tutorial content can be added, versioned, and refreshed
independently of Dashboard releases.

## Scope

- New tutorial gallery surface in the Dashboard: navigation entry, gallery listing,
  and tutorial detail view for the curated tutorials.
- One-click launch mechanics into the user's project:
  - notebook tutorials: open a workbench with the tutorial notebook, running on the
    pinned image;
  - pipeline tutorials: import the pipeline into the user's project.
- Gallery consumption of tutorials packaged per the tutorial packaging format
  (metadata and pinned images drive listing and launch).

Out of scope: the tutorial packaging format itself; authoring tutorial content;
user-facing documentation topics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the tutorial gallery in the Dashboard, when a user opens it, then tutorials
  packaged per the tutorial packaging format are listed with their metadata.
- Given a notebook tutorial in the gallery, when the user launches it into their
  project, then a workbench opens with the tutorial notebook on the pinned image, in
  a single user action.
- Given a pipeline tutorial in the gallery, when the user launches it into their
  project, then the pipeline is imported into the user's project, in a single user
  action.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): the Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can launch a
  tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the notebook, or importing
  the pipeline).

# RHAISTRAT-9019 Decomposition — Curated getting-started tutorial gallery

## Triage Outcome

Full decomposition (not below-threshold, not docs-only). The strategy is well
refined (status: Refinement Done, no open questions), but it explicitly spans three
architecturally distinct work streams with different owners and review processes:
product code (the Dashboard gallery and launch mechanics), substantive content
authoring (the six curated tutorials: notebooks and pipelines), and documentation.
The multiple-distinct-work-streams escape condition for below-threshold applies.
Dashboard requires code changes, so this is not documentation-only.

## Epic List

    E001 --> E003["E003 Notebook tutorials"]
    E001 --> E004["E004 Pipeline tutorial"]

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 → E002 | Rule 13 (build-against artifact) | The packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest) is the artifact the gallery code builds against to list and launch tutorials; the consuming Implementation is serial. |
| E001 → E003 | Rule 12/13 (framework → consumer) | Notebook tutorials are authored in the packaging format; authoring cannot start before the format exists. |
| E001 → E004 | Rule 12/13 (framework → consumer) | The pipeline tutorial is authored in the same packaging format. |

| No edge E002 ↔ E003/E004 | Rule 14 (parallel) | Gallery code and tutorial content are different work products in different repos with no shared build artifact: the gallery is data-driven by the packaging format and the tutorials are content consumed at runtime. End-to-end launch is gated by acceptance criteria on both sides, not by a DAG edge. |

## Work-Stream and Boundary Rationale

- **Code vs. content vs. documentation** (Step 5, Rule 2 work-product type boundary):
  the Dashboard gallery (code), the six curated tutorials (content authoring), and
  the documentation topics are separate epics — different skills, review criteria,
  and PR review cycles, as the strategy's problem statement itself calls out.
- **Spec vs. content** (Step 5, Rule 2 spec-vs-content boundary): the
  packaging-format epic only defines the format and validates it with a minimal
  validation fixture (a small stub exercising metadata, a pinned image reference,
  and a validation manifest — not a usable tutorial). The six real tutorials are
  authored in the content epics, so no two epics produce the same work product.
- **Normative spec vs. user-facing docs** (format-documentation seam): the
  packaging-format epic owns the normative format specification — the
  authoritative definition of the metadata, pinned image references, validation
